Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testReflectionLongArrayArray()` in `ToStringBuilderTest` creates a long[][] array and converts it to a base string representation, then validates the null state of the ToStringStyle registry. The current bug report highlights a memory leak issue due to a `ThreadLocal` field `REGISTRY` in `ToStringStyle` that is created but never removed, with no API to clear or remove the thread local map. The `REGISTRY` is a `ThreadLocal<WeakHashMap<Object, Object>>` storing instances in a thread-local manner. The test calls `validateNullToStringStyleRegistry()`, presumably checking that the registry or the thread local is properly cleared, but there is no provided method to clear or remove the thread local in `ToStringStyle`. Because the `ThreadLocal` remains forever, references are held in container environments, causing memory leaks especially on web application reloads. The lack of an explicit clear or remove method for the thread local field is the root cause of the memory leak and failure to properly reset or clean state in tests or production. Recent similar issues are not directly relevant.

Thus, the bug occurs because `ToStringStyle` uses a thread local registry map but never removes or clears it, causing memory leaks and test failures that expect clean thread local state.

Next, I will check if there are any methods to clear or remove the `REGISTRY` but seems none were found by name queries, hinting that such a method may truly be missing or is named unexpectedly.

The test and reported problem strongly suggest the bug is the missing ability to clear/remove the thread local registry map in `ToStringStyle`. This results in lingering references that cause leaks and failures in tests requiring a clean environment.

Hence, the main fault lies in the handling of the thread local `REGISTRY` in `ToStringStyle`, specifically a missing method or usage pattern to clear or remove it after use.

Suggested location for fix is likely the class `ToStringStyle`, adding registry clearing or removal methods to prevent leaks and test interference.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
